evals.prompt: Propose and rank English titles for the attached economics paper. Give one recommendation and strong alternatives with genuinely different structures.
evals.expected_output: Titles centered on transit support, school attendance/persistence or graduation, and possibly random assignment; no identified-mechanism, welfare-optimum, or universal-policy promise.
expectations: The recommended title truthfully matches the randomized design and studied outcomes.
No title claims an identified liquidity mechanism or optimal universal subsidy.
Alternatives are structurally distinct rather than synonym swaps.
Any Evidence-from construction carries real design or scope information.

evals.prompt: Audit the old title and propose accurate replacements. The output should be useful to an author choosing a final economics-paper title.
evals.expected_output: A clear diagnosis of causal and generic-location overclaiming, followed by conservative titles about remote-work adoption and firm output or linked firm-worker evidence.
expectations: Rejects or repairs the word Causes.
Does not present the United States as an informative Evidence-from tag without justification.
Does not name office-cost savings or a causal productivity effect.
Recommended title remains distinctive and central rather than vague.

evals.prompt: Generate and rank English title candidates for this theory paper. Use theory-appropriate information structures and avoid empirical or policy promises.
evals.expected_output: Concise titles reflecting AI precision, delegation, worker initiative/information, non-monotonicity, or substitutive versus complementary AI without claiming empirical effects.
expectations: No title claims estimation, evidence from data, or a policy experiment.
At least one strong candidate captures the delegation/information mechanism or substitutive-complementary contrast.
Question or colon forms appear only if they improve fit rather than fill a template.
The shortlist contains genuinely different architectures.
